title: dedicated-gpu-pool-scheduling-autoscale-warmup-breadcrumbs
content:
Quick breadcrumbs / scratchpad for the Dedicated GPU pool scheduling/autoscale incident (capacity thrash + cold warmup)

TL;DR
- Users saw increased latency and 502s around 2025-02-14 18:00 UTC.
- Root cause hypothesis: autoscaler launched nodes, pods scheduled, but model containers were cold (weight load + cuda init) causing long startup; autoscaler saw CPU/GPU metrics spike and then scaled down because stabilization/cooldown windows too short => thrash.
- Notes here are experiments/commands, partial outputs, and follow-ups.

Timeline / high-level notes
- 2025-02-14 17:45 UTC: small traffic spike from internal load test (10x qps for ~3m) on pool 'dedicated-gpu-pool-beta'.
- 17:47: autoscaler started adding nodes (3 -> 6).
- 17:49: many pods scheduled, but model-serving containers reported readiness delays (readiness probes failing intermittently ~30-120s).
- 17:52: autoscaler saw ephemeral high GPU usage (because starting containers instantiate CUDA + weights) and then scaled down nodes too quickly; more requests landed on remaining nodes -> more cold starts -> feedback loop.

Commands tried (notes + truncated outputs):
- k get nodes -o wide
  NAME                STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION
  gpu-node-1          Ready    <none>   12d   v1.27.3
  gpu-node-2          Ready    <none>   12d
  gpu-node-3          Ready    <none>   2h
  gpu-node-4          Ready    <none>   2h

- kubectl get pods -n rwd-serving -o wide | grep model-serve
  model-serve-abc    0/1 CrashLoopBackOff   3   2m   10.240.1.5   gpu-node-3
  model-serve-def    1/1 Running           0   90s  10.240.1.8   gpu-node-4

- kubectl describe pod model-serve-abc -n rwd-serving\  (looking for events/readiness failures)
  Events:
    Normal  Scheduled  Successfully assigned rwd-serving/model-serve-abc to gpu-node-3
    Normal  Pulling    Pulling image redwood/model-server:prod-2025-02-10
    Normal  Pulled     Successfully pulled image
    Normal  Created    Created container model-server
    Warning Unhealthy  Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 500

- kubectl logs model-serve-abc -n rwd-serving -c model-server --tail=200\  (truncated)
  [INFO] Initializing CUDA context...
  [INFO] Loading model weights from /models/llama-v2/quantized.pt (size 6.2GB)
  [INFO] Approx time to load weights: 45s
  [WARN] KV cache resize triggered - large sequence
  [ERROR] Readiness probe timed out after 30s

- ssh to node and run nvidia-smi during warmup:
  > nvidia-smi -q -d UTILIZATION
  GPU 0 Utilization: 95% (spikes during model load)

- kubectl top nodes (metrics-server) output around incident (sketchy):
  NAME        CPU(cores)   CPU%   MEMORY(bytes)   MEM%
  gpu-node-3  2500m        80%    60Gi            78%
  gpu-node-4  100m         3%     6Gi             8%

- cluster-autoscaler logs (grep for events):
  I02014 17:47:21 autoscaler.go:...   scale up: request for 3 nodes for deployment/rwd-serving
  I02014 17:51:30 autoscaler.go:...   scale down: removing node gpu-node-3 (low utilization)
  I02014 17:53:02 autoscaler.go:...   scale up: again request for 2 nodes

Hypotheses / root cause threads
1) Cold model weight load + CUDA init causes a short but very high GPU/CPU spike that the autoscaler treats as sustained load and then scales down once the immediate request backlog clears. Because warmup is expensive, reinstated requests cause re-scale -> thrash.
2) Readiness probe is too strict/too short (30s). Containers that are 'starting weights' fail readiness and re-route traffic causing more churn.
3) Autoscaler stabilization/cooldown windows are too short or scale-down thresholds too aggressive for GPU workloads.
4) No warm pool (pre-provisioned nodes with pre-pulled images / preloaded weights) for dedicated pools.
5) Pod distribution/pack scheduling puts many cold containers on same new node leading to simultaneous heavy IO (local disk + PCIe) and appearing as node-level overload.

Immediate mitigations tried / notes
- Increase readiness probe timeout to 120s for model-server: (made change in deployment, rolled to 1 replica first to test) -> improved stability for a single pod (didn't eliminate thrash under high QPS).
- Set minReplicas on HPA to keep baseline pods (from 0 to 2) in the pool for this deployment -> reduced cold starts but increased baseline cost.
- Add / tweak autoscaler stabilization window: scale-down-delay increased from 5m to 10m for cluster-autoscaler config -> reduced oscillation in a follow-up test.
- Pre-pull images on new nodes via DaemonSet (image-prepull) -> images are big so helps but model weight load still dominates.
- Experiment: use initContainer that preloads model weights into a shared tmpfs on node (proof-of-concept) -> reduced individual pod load time from ~45s -> ~8s in lab. But this is hacky and needs guardrails for multi-version models.

Follow-ups / longer-term fixes to propose
- Warm pool / node reservation: maintain a small pool of GPU nodes with models preloaded (or at least pre-pulled image + warm kv cache). Suggest default min_nodes=2 for dedicated pools + an explicit warm_pool_size setting.
- Autoscaler tuning: increase scale-down-unneeded-time and scale-down-utilization-threshold for GPU pools; add scale-down-stabilization for pods to avoid reacting to transient spikes during model load.
- Readiness probe: change to a lightweight HTTP endpoint that returns ready only after model weights + CUDA init complete; increase timeouts. Consider a separate 'serving-ready' vs 'accepting-traffic' probe to avoid dropping into 502s.
- Predictive scaling: if traffic patterns are predictable (e.g., batch jobs, scheduled ingest), use scheduled scaling to pre-warm.
- Model warmup step: when a pod starts, execute a short synthetic request that warms token KV/cache and triggers cache fill (prevent first-customer latency). Mark warmup as non-billable internal traffic.
- Pod placement: prefer spreading cold pods across nodes (PodAntiAffinity) or use bin-packing to avoid many start-ups on same node.
- Instrumentation: add metric for 'model-weight-load-duration' and 'cuda-init-duration' exposed to autoscaler so it can be aware of warmup cost.

Notes about fairness / cost tradeoffs
- Warm pools + pre-warmed nodes cost money; need to expose to customers via config (min_capacity, warm_pool, predictable-scaling windows). For dedicated customers this makes sense.

Things to document for the runbook (next steps)
- Incident description with timeline + commands above.
- Checklist: check readiness probe gRPC/HTTP endpoints; check cluster-autoscaler events; check node GPU utilization via nvidia-smi; check kube-scheduler events for pod backoff; check DaemonSet status for nvidia-device-plugin.
- Quick fixes: bump readiness to 60-120s; set minReplicas=2 for high-SLO deployments; temporarily increase warm_pool to 1 node.
- Longer-term: add warm_pool config to Dedicated offering + autoscaler policy tuning and model warmup primitives in the serving runtime.

Open questions / unknowns
- How often do customers hit this? Is it only synthetic load tests or real traffic spikes? (Need query from analytics: count incidents by customer pool).
- Is the weight-loading I/O bound on node local SSD or network FS? If network FS (NFS/S3 fuse), prefetching to local SSD could help.
- Can we expose a k8s-level annotation so autoscaler treats a new node as \"warming\" for X seconds?

Scratch: rough Kube manifest snippet I tried (readiness tweak)
- original readiness:
  readinessProbe:
    httpGet:
      path: /healthz
      port: 8080
    initialDelaySeconds: 5
    periodSeconds: 10
    timeoutSeconds: 5
    failureThreshold: 3

- new readiness (tested):
  readinessProbe:
    httpGet:
      path: /ready-to-serve
      port: 8080
    initialDelaySeconds: 10
    periodSeconds: 10
    timeoutSeconds: 30
    failureThreshold: 6

Recent small experiments to capture metrics
- add simple gauge metric (prometheus): model_weight_load_seconds_count and _sum from within model-server; recorded ~0.78 quantile = 42s, median = 9s. Shows long tail for cold loads.

Action items
- [ ] Add warm_pool proposal doc for Dedicated product (owners: Lina Chen + Eng infra).
- [ ] Add model_weight_load_seconds metric to serving runtime (owner: Marco Ruiz).
- [ ] Update default readiness probe in model server cookbook and call out warmup cost (owner: Aisha).
- [ ] Run canary with scale-down stabilization = 10m for all GPU pools next week and monitor oscillation.

Random notes / todo (personal)
- Check whether device-plugin restarts during node join (could cause additional delays).
- Run node-local SSD vs NFS model fetch test to measure I/O contribution.
- Talk to product about exposing warm_pool as Dedicated config (price implications).

End of breadcrumbs.
